facts.statement: Sunosuchus fossils date from the Middle Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous, with possible Early Jurassic occurrences.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle Jurassic - Early Cretaceous, (possible Early Jurassic occurrence)

facts.statement: Fossils of Sunosuchus have been found in China, Kyrgyzstan, and Thailand and are Jurassic in age, though some may be Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Fossils are known from China, Kyrgyzstan, and Thailand and are Jurassic in age, although some may be Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Unlike other goniopholidids, the squamosal bone of Sunosuchus is narrow.
facts.quote: Unlike other goniopholidids, the squamosal bone (which is found near the back of the skull) is narrow.

facts.statement: S. junggarensis is the best known species of Sunosuchus, first described in 1996 from the Late Jurassic Junggar Basin in Xinjiang, China.
facts.quote: S. junggarensis is the best known species of Sunosuchus. It was first described in 1996 from the Late Jurassic Junggar Basin in Xinjiang, China.

facts.statement: Sunosuchus material collected from Kyrgyzstan in the 1980s was described in 2000.
facts.quote: Material belonging to Sunosuchus was collected from Kyrgyzstan in the 1980s and was described in 2000.

facts.statement: Specimens of Sunosuchus include many teeth, a dorsal vertebra, vertebral centra, pelvic bones, parts of a fibula and tibia, metatarsals, and ventral and neck osteoderms.
facts.quote: Many teeth were found, as well as a dorsal vertebra and some vertebral centra, some pelvic bones, part of a fibula and tibia, a few metatarsals, and ventral and neck osteoderms.

facts.statement: The only skull parts uncovered in the Kyrgyzstan material were squamosal bones.
facts.quote: The only parts of the skull uncovered were squamosal bones.

facts.statement: S. shunanensis was described in 2005 from the Middle Jurassic of Zigong in Sichuan, China.
facts.quote: A fifth species, S. shunanensis, was described in 2005 from the Middle Jurassic of Zigong in Sichuan, China.

facts.statement: Sunosuchus thailandicus was described from northeastern Thailand in 1980.
facts.quote: Sunosuchus thailandicus was described from northeastern Thailand in 1980.

facts.statement: Sunosuchus thailandicus is known only from a very robust mandible.
facts.quote: It is known only from the mandible, which is very robust.

facts.statement: The tip of the jaw of Sunosuchus thailandicus is spoon-shaped and wider than the portion immediately behind it.
facts.quote: The tip of the jaw is spoon shaped and wider than the portion of the jaw immediately behind it.

facts.statement: A newly discovered specimen suggests that S. thailandicus is distinct enough to be placed in its own genus, Chalawan.
facts.quote: However, a newly discovered specimen showed that S. thailandicus is sufficiently distinct from other nominal species of Sunosuchus to be placed in its own genus, Chalawan.

facts.statement: Sunosuchus was initially classified as a pholidosaurid due to its long, long-snouted jaws.
facts.quote: Sunosuchus was initially classified as a pholidosaurid because its jaws were long, making it a longirostrine, or long-snouted, crocodyliform.

facts.statement: Despite similarities with pholidosaurs, Sunosuchus shares features that ally it with goniopholidids.
facts.quote: Despite the similarities with pholidosaurs, Sunosuchus shares several features with goniopholidids that ally it with the group.

facts.statement: The Kyrgyzstan material represents the westernmost record of Sunosuchus's geographic range.
facts.quote: The material from Kyrgyzstan is the westernmost record of the geographic range of Sunosuchus.

facts.statement: The fauna found with Sunosuchus in Kyrgyzstan, including temnospondyl amphibians and xinjiangchelyid turtles, indicates freshwater environments.
facts.quote: These areas shared a similar fauna that is characterized by crocodyliforms such as Sunosuchus as well as temnospondyl amphibians and xinjiangchelyid turtles, indicating freshwater environments across the region.

facts.statement: The presence of marine hybodont sharks and dipnoans in Kyrgyzstan strata suggests the area was estuarine rather than entirely freshwater.
facts.quote: Marine hybodont sharks and dipnoans are found in the Kyrgyzstan strata, suggesting that the area was estuarine at the time rather than entirely freshwater.

facts.statement: Sunosuchus belongs to the family Goniopholididae.
facts.quote: familia: Goniopholididae

facts.statement: Up to four species have been assigned to the genus Sunosuchus: S. miaoi, S. junggarensis, S. shartegensis, S. shunanensis, and S. thailandicus.
facts.quote: Se han asignado hasta cuatro especies al género: la especie tipo S. miaoi y las especies S. junggarensis, S. shartegensis, S. shunanensis y S. thailandicus.

facts.statement: Sunosuchus had a long, narrow snout and a small cranial vault.
facts.quote: Sunosuchus tenía un largo hocico estrecho y una pequeña bóveda craneana.

facts.statement: The frontal bone of Sunosuchus had a distinctive ridge running along its midline.
facts.quote: El hueso frontal también tenía un distintivo borde corriendo a lo largo de su parte media.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Sunosuchus had a long symphysis where both halves joined.
facts.quote: La mandíbula inferior tenía una larga sínfisis en la que ambas mitades se unían.

facts.statement: The symphysis of Sunosuchus is formed mainly from the mandible bones but also partially from the splenials.
facts.quote: Esta sínfisis se forma mayormente del hueso de las mandíbulas, pero también parcialmente de los espleniales.

facts.statement: S. junggarensis is the best known species of Sunosuchus, originally described in 1996 from Late Jurassic deposits in the Junggar Basin, Xinjiang, China.
facts.quote: S. junggarensis es la especie mejor conocida de Sunosuchus. Fue descrita originalmente en 1996 en depósitos del Jurásico Superior de la Cuenca Junggar en Xinjiang, China.

facts.statement: Specimens of Sunosuchus include many teeth, a dorsal vertebra, vertebral centra, pelvic bones, parts of a fibula and tibia, metacarpals, and ventral and neck osteoderms.
facts.quote: Se hallaron muchos dientes, así como una vértebra dorsal y algunos centros de vértebras, algunos huesos pélvicos, parte de una fíbula y tibia, unos pocos metacarpiano, y osteodermos ventrales y del cuello.

facts.statement: The only skull parts discovered in the Kyrgyzstan material were squamosal bones.
facts.quote: Las únicas partes del cráneo descubiertas fueron huesos escamosales.

facts.statement: S. shunanensis had a longer snout than other species, about three times the length of the postorbital region.
facts.quote: S. shunanensis tenía un hocico más largo que el de las otras especies, siendo alrededor de tres veces la longitud de la región postorbital, la parte del cráneo detrás de los ojos.

facts.statement: S. shunanensis had a wider cranial vault than other species.
facts.quote: También tenía una bóveda craneana más ancha que la de las otras especies.

facts.statement: The skull of S. shunanensis is wider at the back than between the eyes, a trait seen only in this species.
facts.quote: El cráneo es más ancho en la parte posterior en vez de entre los ojos, un rasgo solo visto en S. shunanensis.

facts.statement: There was a distinct depression near the back of each maxilla in S. shunanensis.
facts.quote: Cerca de la parte posterior de cada maxilar había una distintiva depresión.

facts.statement: S. shunanensis had ridges across the skull surface, including a pair at the front of the eye socket on the lacrimals and another along the sides of the bacioccipitals and undersurfaces of the exoccipitals.
facts.quote: Hay unos bordes a través de la superficie del cráneo, un par en el frente de la cuenca orbital sobre el hueso lacrimal, y un segundo junto a los lados del bacioccipital y la superficie inferior del exoccipital en la base del cráneo.

facts.statement: Sunosuchus was initially classified as a pholidosaurid because its elongated jaws made it a long-snouted crocodyliform.
facts.quote: Sunosuchus fue clasificado inicialmente como un folidosáurido debido a que sus mandíbulas alargadas lo vuelven un crocodiloforme longirrostrino.

facts.statement: Despite similarities to pholidosaurids, Sunosuchus shares several traits with goniopholidids that place it in that group.
facts.quote: A pesar de sus similitudes con los folidosáuridos, Sunosuchus comparte varios rasgos con los goniofolídidos que lo incluyen en este grupo.

facts.statement: The traits linking Sunosuchus to goniopholidids might be considered primitive features shared by both goniopholidids and pholidosaurids within Mesosuchia.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estos rasgos pueden ser considerados como plesiomórficos dentro de Mesosuchia, el grupo al cual pertenecen tanto los goniofolídidos como los folidosáuridos.

facts.statement: It is possible that Sunosuchus, or at least S. thailandicus, represents a pholidosaurid that retained ancient characteristics rather than being an advanced goniopholidid.
facts.quote: Si ese es el caso, es posible que Sunosuchus, o al menos S. thailandicus, represente un folidosáurido que retenía características antiguas en vez de ser un goniofolídido avanzado.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Sunosuchus is Goniopholididae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Goniopholididae

facts.statement: Sunosuchus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Sunosuchus lived from the Bajocian to the Tithonian stages, between 170.9 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Tithonian (170.9 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: The fossil material found in Kyrgyzstan represents the westernmost record of Sunosuchus's geographic range.
facts.quote: El material de Kirguistán es el registro más occidental en el rango geográfico de Sunosuchus.

facts.statement: The regions where Sunosuchus fossils were found shared a fauna with temnospondyl amphibians and Xinjiangchelyidae turtles, indicating freshwater ecosystems.
facts.quote: Estas áreas compartían una fauna similar caracterizada por crocodiliformes como Sunosuchus así como anfibios temnospóndilos y tortugas xinjiangquélidas, indicando que había ecosistemas de agua dulce por la región.

facts.statement: The discovery of hybodont sharks and marine dipnoans in the same strata suggests the area was an estuary rather than a purely freshwater environment.
facts.quote: También se han hallado en estos estratos de Kirguistán tiburones hibodóntidos y peces dípneoss marinos, lo que sugiere que el área era un estuario en vez de ser completamente de agua dulce.
